answer: Trust should pass through a prism: it only counts after splitting into independent colours. Score each identity with random walks from a few trusted seeds across the interaction graph; standing equals landing probability. A raven that only talks to its own flock gets no visits, since a sybil cluster reaches honest agents through few attack edges. A falcon that hunts widely, serving unrelated strangers, gathers visits from all directions. Cloning multiplies identities but not attack edges, so each clone's share shrinks, and forging history in every direction costs more than it earns.
